newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Protesters clash with police in Argentine city.
newsitem.headline: Protesters clash with police in Argentine city.

text.p: Argentine police fired tear gas and rubber bullets at stone-throwing protesters Wednesday in Argentina's second city, Cordoba, where state workers demonstrated over unpaid salaries and privatisation plans.
Police sources quoted by state news agency Telam said at least four police officers and four demonstrators were hurt in clashes in the city centre.

The provincial government has angered public sector unions with bills to extend a state of emergency, allowing it to delay payment of state workers' salaries, and to privatise part of the provincial energy firm Epec.
After the morning's violence died down, both bills were being debated in the provincial parliament. About 500 demonstrators waited outside to hear the outcome.
"All of us unions are standing together against this provocative attitude of the government," Walter Grahovac, a member of a teachers' union, told local television.
Cordoba's Radical Party provincial governor, Ramon Mestre, speaking in Brazil on a business trip, condemned the violence which he said "will not resolve our social or economic problems."
